text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on February 10 in history.
1364 - The Treaty of Brno was signed which guaranteed that Tyrol would be kept in the families of the Luxemburgs and Hapsburgs.
1567 - Lord Darnley, second husband of Mary Queen of Scots, was murdered.
1763 - The Peace of Paris between Britain, France and Spain ended the Seven Years War. Canada was ceded to Britain, France received various West Indies possessions and Spain won Louisiana and Havana.
1775 - Charles Lamb, English writer and essayist best known for his "Essays of Elia", born.
1824 - Samuel Plimsoll, English social reformer, born; he also devised the Plimsoll Line, which regulated the weight ships could safely carry.
1837 - Alexander Pushkin, Russian poet and novelist, killed in a duel. Regarded as Russia's greatest poet, his works include the historical tragedy "Boris Godunov".
1840 - Queen Victoria of England married Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg.
1841 - The Act of Union uniting Upper and Lower Canada, signed on this day in 1840, came into effect.
1890 - Boris Pasternak, Russian author of "Dr Zhivago", born.
1893 - Jimmy Durante, U.S. vaudeville performer and comedian, born.
1894 - Harold Macmillan, British statesman and Conservative Prime Minister, born; he succeeded Anthony Eden in 1957 and steered the Conservatives to electoral success two years later.
1898 - Bertold Brecht, German poet and playwright, born. His plays include "The Threepenny Opera", "Mother Courage", and "The Caucasian Chalk Circle".
1932 - Edgar Wallace, British author of thrillers, died.
1942 - Glenn Miller received the first ever gold disc for selling one million copies of "Chatanooga Choo Choo".
1962 - Francis Gary Powers, U.S. pilot of a U-2 plane shot down over the Soviet Union and imprisoned in 1960, was exchanged for KGB agent Rudolf Abel in Berlin.
1970 - Arab terrorists killed one Israeli and wounded 10 others in an attack on an El Al airliner at Munich.
1975 - Pakistan banned the opposition National Awami Party and arrested its leaders.
1977 - Physicist Yuri Orlov, a leader of a Soviet dissident group monitoring implementation of the 1975 Helsinki human rights accord, was arrested.
1981 - Leopoldo Calvo Sotelo was named as Spanish prime minister by King Juan Carlos.
1989 - Michael Manley became Prime Minister of Jamaica.
1991 - Lithuanians voted overwhelmingly for independence from the Soviet Union. Parliament had already declared independence in March 1990
1992 - Alex Haley, U.S. author of the book "Roots", died.
1994 - Russia called for a Security Council meeting to consider putting Sarajevo under U.N. administration.
1996 - Voters in a referendum in the Central Asian state of Kyrgyzstan approved proposals to grant extra powers to reformist President Askar Akayev.
1996 - An IBM computer called Deep Blue made chess history by comfortably beating world champion Garry Kasparov, a machine's first victory under classic tournament rules.
